payload.instruction: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk

program.instruction: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
program.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

requirements.text: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
requirements.source_phrase: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk

outcomes.description: Transform the image into a chalk drawing.
outcomes.target: The image is rendered as a drawing made from chalk, rather than merely showing an unrelated edit or a partial chalk effect.
outcomes.reference: The input image and the edited image; compare whether the edited image has the appearance of a chalk-made drawing.

nodes.question: Does convincing chalk mark-making serve as the rendering medium for both the giraffes and the surrounding scene?
nodes.criteria: Pass if identifiable powdery or broken strokes, chalk-like contours and rubbed shading visibly render both the giraffes and their surroundings. Assess actual marks and their relationship to depicted forms, not merely an overall soft or grainy appearance. Fail if the apparent chalk medium consists only of uniform grain, blur or smearing, or if convincing chalk rendering is confined to isolated outlines while the remaining scene lacks it. Color is permitted, and neither monochrome nor a blackboard background is required. Recognizable anatomy does not itself indicate failure. Return unknown only when visual evidence is unavailable or genuinely insufficient; transport or schema failures are not negative visual evidence.
nodes.binding: Compare the input and edited images for the requested chalk-drawing appearance, inspecting marks and shading on the giraffes, vegetation and ground.

nodes.question: Are both the giraffes and the surrounding environment consistently represented as drawn forms rather than photographic forms beneath a surface effect?
nodes.criteria: Pass if drawn contours, interior marks and shading represent the principal subjects and the surrounding vegetation, ground and background, so substantial scene regions no longer rely on photographic surface detail or photographic tonal modeling. Inspect the giraffes' bodies and markings as well as the full environment; sketch-like silhouettes alone do not establish this condition. Fail if substantial regions retain photographic rendering beneath added grain, outlined edges or smudging, even when other regions have been convincingly drawn. Background blur or loss of detail alone does not establish drawn representation. Recognizable anatomy, retained composition, accurate markings, fine drawn detail and retained colors are permitted; source resemblance alone is not evidence of photographic rendering. Return unknown only when the images are unavailable or genuinely insufficient to distinguish the rendering, not merely because evidence differs across regions.
nodes.binding: Compare the input and edited images for the requested transformation into a chalk-made drawing, examining the giraffes' bodies and markings as well as the vegetation, ground and background.

program.checker_template: Evaluate ONE independent required condition against the SOURCE and EDITED images. No reference label, previous answers or optimization feedback is supplied. Return pass if the condition is satisfied, fail if it is not satisfied, or unknown if the evidence cannot establish an answer. Inspect only this saved condition, its criteria and binding. Report factual evidence and confidence (0..1 or null). A pass means satisfaction of THIS condition, not an overall edit label. Do not anticipate the optimizer's target. Missing evidence or transport/schema failures must not become a negative observation. The final overall label is computed by code; you never supply it.

d1_drawn_representation: The binding is too vague and its “photographic forms beneath a surface effect” phrasing may bias the decision toward treating chalk texture, blur, or grain as evidence of failure. Keep the comparison anchored to the requested chalk drawing, and make the decision inspect both giraffes and the environment for actual drawn contours, marks, and shading versus retained photographic modeling; texture or smudging alone is not decisive. The traces show a real borderline distinction: the giraffes have drawn outlines and marks, while their bodies retain photographic tonal structure and much of the environment is blurred or smeared rather than clearly re-rendered. Other runs judge broad chalk-like environmental strokes sufficient. Clarify how to weigh these regions against the criterion that substantial scene areas must read as drawn, without letting one convincing region stand in for the whole scene or treating source resemblance as proof of photographic rendering. Preserve the partial-progress distinction: visible chalk-drawing changes count as progress, but do not automatically establish complete fulfillment. All traces are valid observations with no dependency or transport failures; the disagreement is semantic, not missing evidence. Repeated high-confidence variation is a calibration signal, not grounds to force a label.
d1_chalk_medium: Make the binding explicitly compare the source and edit for the requested chalk-drawing transformation, and assess the giraffes and substantial surrounding regions separately before judging the scene as a whole. Distinguish form-following chalk marks, broken contours, and rubbed shading from mere grain, blur, or smearing; do not treat either recognizable anatomy or resemblance to the source as proof of failure. The edit visibly changes the scene with chalk-like outlines and texture, but the giraffes retain detailed tonal modeling and much of the environment reads as broad smears, so clarify how mixed evidence bears on completion: visible requested progress is not automatically full fulfillment, and one region should not stand in for both. Keep the decision calibrated to the stated criteria rather than forcing a label. Traces are valid and repeated; there are no transport, schema, or dependency failures, so focus on semantic weighting and confidence calibration.

Existing assessments inconsistently distinguish these drawn marks from blur and treat smooth tonal shading as photographic evidence. Clarify both conditions using form-linked visual evidence, while retaining separate requirements for chalk medium and drawn representation across the scene.

decisions.question: Does chalk-like mark-making render both giraffes and the substantial surrounding scene?
decisions.criteria: Pass if chalk-like contours, powdery or broken strokes, layered strokes, or rubbed chalk shading visibly describe both giraffes and substantial surrounding regions. These are alternative manifestations of chalk, not features that must all occur everywhere. Broad rubbed shading can qualify when its direction, boundaries, layering or pigment variation describes depicted forms; uniform grain or loss of sharpness alone cannot. Inspect the giraffes separately from the vegetation, hills, sky and ground: convincing marks in one region cannot substitute for chalk rendering in the other. Fail if either the giraffes or substantial surrounding regions are rendered only by photographic detail, generic grain, blur or smearing without form-describing chalk marks. Color, smooth blended passages, recognizable anatomy and retained composition are permitted. Return unknown only if visual evidence is unavailable or genuinely insufficient; transport or schema failures are not visual failures.
decisions.binding: Compare the supplied SOURCE and EDITED images for the requested transformation into a drawing made from chalk. Inspect the contours, spots and shading of both giraffes, then inspect vegetation, hills, sky and ground for form-describing chalk strokes or rubbed shading rather than merely changed texture.

decisions.question: Are both giraffes and the substantial surrounding scene represented through drawn contours, interior marks and shading rather than retained photographic rendering?
decisions.criteria: Pass if drawn contours, interior marks and constructed shading represent both giraffes and substantial surrounding regions. Evaluate the giraffes' bodies, spots and legs separately from the vegetation, hills, sky and ground; neither region alone establishes satisfaction. Broad directional strokes and blended drawn shading may represent simplified environmental forms without preserving fine detail. Fail if substantial areas in either region still depend on retained photographic surface detail or photographic modeling, with only added outlines, grain or blur. Distinguish photographic modeling through retained source-specific detail and tonal structure not re-expressed by drawn marks; accurate anatomy, detailed spots, smooth gradients, dark shading and source resemblance are not by themselves proof of photographic rendering. Texture and smudging alone establish neither drawing nor photography. Return unknown only when evidence is unavailable or genuinely insufficient to distinguish the rendering, not simply because different regions provide different evidence.
decisions.binding: Compare the supplied SOURCE and EDITED images for the requested chalk-drawing transformation. Examine whether the giraffes' contours, body shading and markings are re-expressed as drawn forms, and whether vegetation, hills, sky and ground are independently represented by drawn marks and shading rather than merely softened source detail.
